ai.literal: Even in the condition of support being lost, cherishing old relationships exists only with kinsmen.
ai.translation: Even when one's wealth and support are entirely lost, the quality of cherishing old relationships is found only among one's kinsmen.
ai.modern: ஆதரவு அல்லது செல்வம் இல்லாத வறுமை நிலையிலும், பழைய உறவைப் போற்றிப் பாராட்டும் குணம் சுற்றத்தாரிடமே உண்டு.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the unique value of relatives during times of adversity. The word 'paṟṟu' here refers to wealth or support, and 'aṟṟa kaṇṇum' means 'even when that support is completely lost'. While others might abandon a person who has lost their fortune, true kinsmen will still cherish and honor their long-standing relationship ('paḻaimai pārāṭṭutal'). This enduring loyalty is a defining characteristic found only ('kaṇṇē') among one's relatives.

ai.literal: If one obtains relatives whose affection does not cease, it will give many prosperities that do not cease to bud.
ai.translation: If one is blessed with relatives whose affection never wanes, it will yield many forms of ever-budding prosperity.
ai.modern: அன்பு குறையாத சுற்றத்தாரைப் பெறின், அது என்றும் புதிய அரும்புகள் போலத் தோன்றி வளரும் பல செல்வங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense value of having loyal and loving relatives. The word 'viruppara' refers to affection that never ceases or diminishes. The term 'aruppara' literally means 'without the buds ceasing', symbolizing continuous, fresh growth. The poet states that if a person secures a circle of relatives whose love is constant, that relationship itself becomes the source of endless, ever-renewing wealth and well-being.

ai.literal: The life of one who does not mingle is like a pond's expanse filled with water without an embankment.
ai.translation: The life of one who does not mingle lovingly with his relatives is like a wide pond filled with water that has no retaining bank.
ai.modern: சுற்றத்தாருடன் கலந்து பழகாதவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, கரையில்லாமல் நீர் நிறைந்த குளத்தைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of maintaining close and affectionate relationships with one's relatives. The poet compares the life of a person who does not mingle or socialize with his kin to a pond filled with water but lacking a protective embankment. Just as water in a bankless pond quickly drains away and goes to waste, the wealth and prosperity of a man who isolates himself from his relatives will not endure. Thus, relatives act as the protective banks that preserve and sustain one's life and resources.

ai.literal: By relatives, to be surrounded, living, wealth indeed, by acquiring, obtained benefit.
ai.translation: Living surrounded by one's relatives is the true benefit obtained by acquiring wealth.
ai.modern: தன் சுற்றத்தாரால் சூழப்பட்டு வாழும் வாழ்க்கை முறையே, ஒருவன் செல்வத்தைப் பெற்றதனால் அடையும் உண்மையான பயனாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the ultimate purpose of acquiring material wealth. The author states that the real fruit (பயன்) of possessing wealth (செல்வம்) is the ability to live a life surrounded (சுற்றப்பட) and supported by one's relatives (சுற்றம்). The word 'ஒழுகல்' refers to one's conduct and way of living. Thus, wealth is not an end in itself, but a means to foster and cherish a close-knit community of kinsmen.

ai.literal: And giving and pleasant words if one practices, by piled-up relatives to be surrounded one will undergo.
ai.translation: If one practices both generosity and pleasant speech, one will be surrounded by an ever-growing, multi-layered circle of relatives.
ai.modern: கொடைத் தன்மையையும் இனிய சொற்களைப் பேசுதலையும் ஒருவன் கடைப்பிடித்தால், அவன் பல அடுக்குகளாகப் பெருகிய சுற்றத்தாரால் சூழப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how a person can gather and retain a large, supportive circle of relatives and friends. The two essential qualities required are generosity (கொடுத்தல்) and speaking sweet, pleasant words (இன்சொல்). If a person consistently practices these virtues, their relatives will gather around them in multiple, closely-knit layers (அடுக்கிய சுற்றம்). The image of 'piled-up' or 'layered' relatives suggests an abundant, protective, and ever-expanding circle of kin who stand by the individual.

ai.literal: One of great generosity, who does not cherish anger, than him, those who have surrounding relations, on this great earth, there is none.
ai.translation: There is no one on this vast earth who possesses more surrounding kinsmen than a person of great generosity who does not harbor anger.
ai.modern: பெரிய கொடையாளனாகவும், கோபத்தைக் கொள்ளாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனை விட, அதிகமான சுற்றத்தாரைப் பெற்றவர் இந்த பெரிய உலகத்தில் யாரும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the two essential qualities required to attract and retain a large circle of relatives and friends: boundless generosity and freedom from anger. A person who gives freely to those in need and never harbors resentment or anger will naturally draw people toward them. The poet asserts that such an individual will have the largest network of supportive relations on earth. The word 'maruṅku' refers to one's side or surrounding relations, emphasizing how these virtues keep people closely bound to one's side.

ai.literal: The crow, without concealing, calling out eats; prosperity also to such natured people only exists.
ai.translation: Crows do not hide their food but call out to their kind to share it; prosperity likewise abides only with those who possess such a sharing nature.
ai.modern: காகம் தனக்குக் கிடைத்த உணவை மறைக்காமல் தன் சுற்றத்தைக் கூவி அழைத்து உண்ணும். அது போன்ற பகிர்ந்துண்ணும் குணம் உடையவர்களுக்கே செல்வமும் சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the simple, everyday behavior of a crow to teach a profound lesson on cherishing one's kinsmen. The word 'கரவா' means without hiding or keeping secrets, and 'கரைந்து' refers to the crow's habit of cawing to summon its flock when it finds food. The poet states that 'ஆக்கம்' (wealth or prosperity) will only come to and stay with ('உள') those who share the crow's generous nature ('அன்ன நீரார்க்கே'). True prosperity does not belong to the selfish, but to those who actively call upon their relatives and community to share in their good fortune.

ai.literal: Without looking commonly, if the king looks according to merit, seeking that, many will live.
ai.translation: If a ruler does not look upon everyone with a common, indifferent eye but regards each according to their specific merit, many will gather and live under his protective care.
ai.modern: அனைவரையும் பொதுவாகப் பார்க்காமல், அரசன் அவரவர் தகுதிக்கு ஏற்ப ஆராய்ந்து நோக்கினால், அந்த அன்பை நாடி அவனோடு கூடி வாழ்பவர் பலர் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how a leader can gather and retain a large circle of supportive kinsmen and followers. If a king treats everyone with a flat, indifferent equality, he fails to appreciate individual worth. Instead, when he regards people according to their distinct merit and value, people recognize this appreciation. Seeking that supportive and discerning gaze, many will gladly come to live under his patronage.

ai.literal: Those who were relations and abandoned their own, their kinship, when the reason for dislike is without, will return.
ai.translation: Those who were once relations and abandoned their family will return to that kinship of their own accord when the cause of their dislike is gone.
ai.modern: உறவினர்களாக இருந்து பிரிந்து சென்றவர்கள், தங்களுக்குள் இருந்த வெறுப்புக்கான காரணம் நீங்கியவுடன், மீண்டும் உறவினர்களாகத் தேடி வருவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes how estranged relatives can be reunited. It explains that when those who were once close kinsmen (தமராகி) abandon their family (தற்றுறந்தார்), they will return (வரும்) to the fold of kinship (சுற்றம்). This reunion happens naturally once the underlying cause (காரணம்) for their dislike or lack of harmony (அமராமை) is removed or ceases to exist (இன்றி). The poet emphasizes that relationships are resilient, and once misunderstandings are cleared, unity is restored.

ai.literal: From the presence having separated, due to a reason him who came back, the king, having carefully examined, having waited, having evaluated, should accept.
ai.translation: When a relative who had departed from one's presence returns with a specific reason, the king should carefully examine the cause, wait patiently, evaluate their intent, and then accept them back.
ai.modern: தன்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்று, பின்னர் ஒரு காரணத்தோடு திரும்பி வந்தவனை, அரசன் ஆராய்ந்து, பொறுத்திருந்து, அவனது தகுதியை எண்ணிப் பார்த்து மீண்டும் சேர்த்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises a leader on how to receive a relative or associate who previously left but has now returned. The word 'உழை' refers to one's close presence or side, indicating a former close companion. When such a person returns due to a specific cause ('காரணத்தின்'), the leader must not act in haste. Instead, they must carefully examine the circumstances ('இழைத்து'), wait and observe patiently ('இருந்து'), and thoroughly evaluate the person's true intent ('எண்ணி') before deciding to accept them back ('கொளல்').
